Tools
HubSpot/CRM · Google Workspace · Loom · Zoom · LinkedIn Sales Nav · Heyreach · AI Tools (ChatGPT, Claude)


ABOUT KASPARRO
Kasparro is an AI Visibility platform. We help brands get discovered, recommended, and chosen by AI engines — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode. As buyers increasingly start their research inside AI assistants, being recommended (or ignored) by those engines becomes a commercial issue. That’s the gap we close.
We run structured, evidence-backed audits that score how AI systems see a brand — across visibility, recommendation rate, sentiment, citations, and share of voice. Then we help brands fix what’s broken so they get recommended, not ignored. We work across verticals: consumer electronics, personal care, wellness, B2B SaaS, AI, fintech — any brand whose buyers are researching inside AI engines.
We’re backed by experienced founders, CMOs, and angels. We’re small, fast-moving, and building quickly in HSR Layout, Bengaluru. The people who join now will shape what this company becomes.

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
AI engines are forming product shortlists before buyers ever visit a brand’s website. When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity “what’s the best CRM for a 50-person sales team?” or “which vitamin C serum works for oily skin?” — the AI names two or three brands. Everyone else is invisible. There is no second page in an AI answer.
We now have a working product, paying clients, and a pipeline of qualified prospects from outbound and inbound. What we don’t have is a dedicated closer. Today, the founder runs every demo. That doesn’t scale. This role exists to own the revenue line — from qualified lead to signed contract — and eventually to build the sales function from the ground up.

WHAT THE SALE LOOKS LIKE
The buyer. VP Marketing, Head of E-commerce, Head of Growth, or founder at companies doing $10M–$100M+ in revenue. These are people who own acquisition budgets, feel organic traffic declining, and have started noticing that AI gives weird or incomplete answers about their brand. They’re on LinkedIn, they’re in industry Slacks, and most of them don’t yet know that “AI visibility” is a category.
The pipeline. You inherit a qualified pipeline from two sources: (1) cold outbound run by our GTM team via personalized email and LinkedIn sequences, and (2) warm inbound from content, AI Shelf Check teardowns, and audit-led marketing. You don’t need to build a list or write cold emails. You pick up where the SDR leaves off — and close.
The cycle. Typically 2–4 weeks for mid-market deals, longer for enterprise. Discovery call → audit walkthrough (you present the brand’s AI visibility scores with real data) → proposal → negotiation → close. The audit is the sales weapon — when a VP Marketing sees that their brand scores 28/100 on non-branded queries while their competitor scores 71, the conversation shifts from “why should I care?” to “what do we fix first?”
The deal. $10–30K annual contract value. Land-and-expand motion — most clients start with an audit and monitoring engagement, then expand into structured data, content fixes, and authority building. Your job is to land the first contract; expansion revenue follows from delivery quality.
The geography. US and India. US prospects are the larger pipeline — you’ll run demos in the evening IST (some 7 PM–12 AM calls, not every day) and manage asynchronous follow-ups. India meetings are in-person or daytime video calls. You need to be comfortable operating across both.

WHAT YOU OWN
The demo. You run every qualified demo from day 30 onward. Discovery, needs assessment, audit walkthrough, objection handling, next-step setting. You make the buyer see what they’re losing by being invisible to AI — with their own data, not a generic pitch.
The close. Proposal creation, pricing negotiation, contract execution. You own the full cycle from qualified opportunity to signed deal. No one else is closing for you.
The handoff. Clean handoff to the Solutions Engineer post-close. Client expectations set correctly. No overpromising to win the deal and then leaving delivery to clean up.
The feedback loop. You are the closest person to the buyer’s voice. What objections come up repeatedly? Which ICP segments convert fastest? What messaging makes people lean in vs tune out? You feed this back to the founder and the GTM team — and it shapes the playbook.
The CRM. Pipeline hygiene, deal stage accuracy, activity logging, forecast updates. If it’s not in the CRM, it didn’t happen.

YOUR FIRST 12 MONTHS
Month 1
Learn the product, the buyer, the pitch
Shadow the founder on live demos. Run the audit on 5 brands yourself so you can explain every score. Study closed-won and closed-lost deals. Understand why a VP Marketing in the US cares about AI visibility and what makes them say yes.
Months 2–3
Run demos, close your first deals
Take over warm demos from the outbound pipeline. Run the full cycle: discovery call, audit walkthrough, proposal, negotiation, close. The founder is in the room for your first 5 demos, then you fly solo. Target: 4–5 closed deals.
Months 4–6
Own the number
You have a pipeline, a rhythm, and a quota. You’re running 5 demos a week — 20–25 demos a month. You’re closing 4–5 deals per month at ~$20K ACV, generating $75–100K in new ACV monthly. You’re feeding objection patterns and ICP refinements back to the GTM team. You’re starting to shape how Kasparro sells, not just executing a playbook someone else wrote.
Year 1+
Build the function
Sales Lead → Head of Sales. You hire your first SDR. You own the full revenue engine: pipeline, demos, proposals, contracts, expansion. The function is yours.


WHO THIS IS FOR
You’ve done 2–4 years in B2B SaaS sales. You might be an SDR who’s been promoted to AE and closed real revenue, or a junior AE at a funded startup who’s ready for more ownership. Either way, you’ve built pipeline, navigated multi-stakeholder deals, and have a feel for when a prospect is genuinely interested vs politely stalling.
You’ve closed $500K+ in cumulative ACV across the last 12 months. You know what it takes to move a deal from first call to signed contract. You’ve worked a CRM with discipline — not because someone audited it, but because you understood that pipeline accuracy is how you forecast your own quarter.
Beyond the numbers, what matters is:
You can run a 30-minute demo without a script. You listen first, adapt on the fly, and make the buyer feel like the conversation was built for them. You ask sharper questions than you give pitches.
You sell with data, not charm. Our sale is diagnostic-led. You walk a buyer through their brand’s AI visibility scores and let the evidence create urgency. If you’re used to consultative, insight-led, data-forward selling, you’ll feel at home.
You think analytically about ICP. You don’t just work a list — you think about why certain segments convert, which buyer personas respond to which angles, and how to prioritize your pipeline based on fit signals, not just deal size. You understand that selling to a VP Marketing at a $50M D2C brand is a different conversation than selling to a Head of Growth at a $10M SaaS company — and you adjust.
You’re comfortable with US clients. Clear spoken English, cultural fluency, no hesitation on a Zoom call with a VP in San Francisco. This isn’t about accent — it’s about confidence and calibration.
You’re curious about AI and how it changes buying behavior. You don’t need to be an AI expert. But you should have asked an AI chatbot for a product recommendation at least once and wondered how it picked those brands.
You can handle ambiguity. There is no 40-page sales playbook. There is a product that works, a founder who sells well, and a market that’s waking up. You’ll be building the playbook as you go — not following one.

Bonus: Prior experience selling to marketing or growth leaders. Familiarity with SEO, martech, or analytics tools. Experience at a startup that was creating a new category rather than competing in an established one.

WHAT’S HARD ABOUT THIS ROLE
You’re selling a category most buyers don’t know exists yet. AI visibility is not a line item in anyone’s budget today. Your job is to make it one. That means the first 30 seconds of every conversation is education, not pitch. If you need a warm market where buyers already know what they’re shopping for, this isn’t it.
The team is small. You’ll work directly with the founder and a lean GTM squad. There is no sales ops team formatting your proposals, no enablement team building your battle cards, no RevOps person cleaning your CRM. You do your own work. The upside is that you shape everything — the downside is that everything is yours to shape.
Evening and late-night calls are part of the job. Not every day, but a US-facing sales role from Bengaluru means some 7 PM–12 AM calls. If you want a strict 9-to-6, this won’t work.

WHAT YOU GET
₹12–15 LPA fixed — based on experience and calibration during the process.
₹3–5 LPA variable — tied to pipeline and closed revenue milestones. Structured so you earn meaningfully from Month 3.
₹3–5 LPA in ESOPs — real equity in a company building infrastructure for a market that didn’t exist two years ago.
Total CTC: ₹18–25 LPA (fixed + variable + equity).

Founding sales seat. You’re not filling a vacancy in a 10-person sales team. You’re building the function. The path from here is Sales Lead → Head of Sales → VP Revenue as the company scales.
Full-funnel ownership. You don’t just close — you work across the entire funnel from qualified lead to signed contract to clean handoff. You see how pipeline is built, how deals move, how delivery starts. That end-to-end exposure is rare in a sales role and it makes you a significantly better operator.
Front seat to the AI commerce shift. AI is rewriting how buyers discover and choose products. You’ll be selling at the center of that shift — working with brands across categories to understand how AI engines form recommendations, what breaks, and what to fix. The market knowledge you build here doesn’t exist in any textbook yet.
AI tools as daily infrastructure. You’ll use ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools not as novelty but as core workflow — for research, prospecting, pitch prep, deal analysis, and client communication. You’ll upskill faster here than in any structured training program.
Shaping the future of AI-led marketing and brand. The category of AI visibility is being defined right now. The playbooks, the frameworks, the language — you’ll help build it. The brands you close and the patterns you surface will directly shape how the industry thinks about AI-mediated commerce.
Direct founder exposure. You’ll sit in on positioning decisions, pricing conversations, ICP refinement, and GTM strategy — not because you’re invited as a guest, but because you’re a core part of those decisions.
